To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

multirate service mechanisms provide better performance than single-rate service mechanisms for bursty traffic, and that the benefits of multirate service are further enhanced if the service quality need not always be guaranteed.

multirate scheduling can significantly improve the utilization of ATM networks and that the benefits of multirate scheduling are more significant in a network environment than in a single node environment.

(1) a multirate server outperforms a single-rate server and a CBR server in terms of the size of the region in which the server can admit a given number of connections, and (2) the performance of a multirate server is further improved when it is combined with a predictive service mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the performance of ATM networks by exploiting the multiplexing capabilities of multirate service.
the design of a multirate service that allows a session's bandwidth to be dynamically adjusted in response to the traffic characteristics of that session.
improving the performance of bursty traffic by exploiting the multiplexing capabilities of ATM networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multirate service is a promising approach to the design of ATM schedulers.
a multirate server is a better alternative to single-rate servers, especially when the traffic is bursty and when service quality guarantees are not necessary.
a combination of multirate and predictive service is the most efficient mechanism for multiplexing video traffic in ATM networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multirate servers are able to exploit the multiplexer's ability to provide quality of service guarantees while allowing the applications to exploit the multiplicity of rates available to them.
multirate service is an attractive mechanism to exploit the multiplicity gains of ATM.

multirate service can improve the performance of VBR video traffic by a factor of 1.5 over single-rate service, and that it can improve the performance by another factor of 2.0 over single-rate service when combined with predictive service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multirate server is a powerful mechanism for exploiting multiplexing gains in ATM networks.
a multirate service can be designed to exploit the multiplexer gains of ATM, without compromising the quality of service guarantees.
multirate service can improve the utilization of ATM networks and provide better service to applications generating bursty data.
